The Wetlands is a large, wet region below Stonewrought Dam and north of Loch Modan, covered with small rivers, lakes, and ponds. Bordered on three sides by mountains, the Wetlands are open to the Great Sea to the west. Adventurers seeking a route to the Wetlands must either come through sieged Dun Algaz from Loch Modan or cross the damaged Thandol Span from the Arathi Highlands.
The Wetlands is a vast, cold swamp. Mists cloak the ground, and the overcast sky makes the land a uniform gray. Many Ironforge strongholds once stood in this region, but war has reduced them to rubble. Wild creatures, murlocs and orcs of Dragonmaw clan now control the land. The main bastion of Alliance's power in the region, the Menethil Harbor, has partially sunk and flooded due to irregular tectonic activity caused by the Shattering. The night elves also maintain a small holdout in the eastern parts, the Greenwarden's Grove - home to the fabled Rethiel the Greenwarden.

Bordered on three sides by mountains, the Wetlands are open to the [[Great Sea]] to the west. Adventurers seeking a route to the Wetlands must either come through sieged [[Dun Algaz]] from Loch Modan or cross the damaged [[Thandol Span]] from the [[Arathi Highlands]]. The Wetlands is a vast, cold swamp. Mists cloak the ground, and the overcast sky makes the land a uniform gray. Many Ironforge strongholds once stood in this region, but war has reduced them to rubble. Wild creatures, [[murloc]]s and [[orc]]s of [[Dragonmaw clan]] now control the land. The main bastion of [[Alliance]]'s power in the region, the [[Menethil Harbor]], has partially sunk and flooded due to irregular tectonic activity caused by the [[Cataclysm (event)|Shattering]]. The [[Night elf|night elves]] also maintain a small holdout in the eastern parts, the [[Greenwarden's Grove]] - home to the fabled [[Rethiel the Greenwarden]]. ==History== {{Stub/Lore-section|WoW, NotD, Cata.}} [[File:Dun Modr.jpg|thumb|[[Dun Modr]]]] After the original [[Dwarf|dwarven]] kingdom of Ironforge was left shattered by infighting, the [[Wildhammer dwarf|Wildhammer dwarves]] traveled northeast and founded their new capital city in the mountains of [[Grim Batol]]. When the [[War of the Three Hammers]] reignited, the [[Dark Iron dwarf|Dark Irons]] invaded Grim Batol and almost succeeded in taking full control of it, but were driven back at the last minute. Seeing their city irremediably tainted and uninhabitable, the majority of the Wildhammers turned north to settle in the [[Hinterlands]], while the rest settled in the region of [[Northeron]], not far from their cursed former home.{{Ref WoWCV1|154|156}} After the war the dwarves of [[Ironforge]] sought to retain relations and trade with their Wildhammer cousins and built the [[Thandol Span]] to bridge the gap between [[Khaz Modan]] and [[Lordaeron]] and to serve as both an economic and a symbolic bridge between the dwarven territories.[[War of the Three Hammers (History of Warcraft)]]{{Ref WoWCV1|156}} For years, the marshland was considered to be [[murloc]]-infested.{{Ref WoWCodex|31}} ===Second War=== When the [[Second War]] started several dwarven clans numbering hundreds of members lived in the area of the Wetlands. [[Orgrim Doomhammer]] chose [[Menethil Harbor|a small island]] in [[Baradin Bay]] to be the place where his invasion fleet would be built. Sailing straight to the [[Hillsbrad Foothills]] would let the [[Old Horde]] avoid the ground defenses of the nascent [[Alliance of Lordaeron]].{{Ref WoWCV2|151}} The [[Bleeding Hollow clan]] was left behind to guard the [[Oil refinery|refinement operations]] of the Horde,''[[Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness]]'' manual, ''[[Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness manual#Bleeding Hollow Clan|Clans of the Horde]]'', Bleeding Hollow Clan while [[Dragonmaw clan]] established itself in Grim Batol. The region suffered greatly from this occupation: wildlife became scarce as both the orcs and their dragons thrived heavily on fresh meat, and despoiled badlands became more common as plants themselves suffered.''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', chapter 10 After the Second War, the area was reconquered and Doomhammer's port was rebuilt as an Alliance settlement named [[Menethil Harbor]] in honor of the king of [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]], [[Terenas Menethil II]]. The forces of the [[Horde of Draenor]] later attacked the harbor in order to steal ships and set sail for the [[Tomb of Sargeras]].{{Ref WoWCV2|188}} ===Battle of Grim Batol=== The Dragonmaw clan in the region was eventually subject to the wrath of the [[red dragonflight]] who, when freed of their enslavement from the orcs during the [[Battle of Grim Batol]], attacked them. Many of the orcs had died in the battle, and the terrified survivors had scattered into the wilds. They would remain a threat on Azeroth, but they would never truly regain their former power.{{Ref WoWCV3|23}} In the aftermath, most assumed that the fortress' evil legacy had been eradicated. However, the dwarves sensed that a darkness still permeated the mountain and so left shortly after the orcs' defeat. Alexstrasza and her consort [[Korialstrasz]] decided that it was the [[red dragonflight]]'s duty to seal off Grim Batol and sent red dragonkin forces to stand guard around the mountain and prevent anyone from entering.''[[Night of the Dragon]]'', chapter 1, pg. 10 ===World of Warcraft=== {{Wow-section}} While [[Ironforge (kingdom)|Ironforge]] soldiers gave their lives in far-off territories in the name of the [[Alliance]], the dwarven lands fell prey to the evil deeds of the [[Dark Iron clan|Dark Iron dwarves]]. Led by a powerful warlock named [[Balgaras the Foul]], they laid waste to the [[Thandol Span]], and southern [[Dun Modr]] fell soon after.[[The Dark Iron War]] While they normally hid in the hills, a group of Dragonmaw expanded into [[Dun Algaz]], threatening to cut off [[Loch Modan]] from [[Menethil Harbor]] in the Wetlands.[[The Algaz Gauntlet]] ===Cataclysm=== {{Cata-section}} [[File:Menethil Harbor after Cataclysm.jpg|thumb|[[Menethil Harbor]] after the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]].]] The [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] caused a flood of the western part of the Wetlands and of [[Menethil Harbor]], sweeping a good number of ocean dwellers with it.[[When Life Gives You Crabs]] The flood from [[Loch Modan]]'s [[Loch]] distressed with local wildlife's and brought [[threshadon]]s as well.[[Thresh Out of Luck]] After they learned of [[Rethiel the Greenwarden]] from a local [[Dwarf|dwarven]] legend, which told of a [[Bog beast|plant-man]] acting as protector of the region, the [[Night elf|night elves]] came to the Wetlands to find him and ended up settling down. They eventually founded the [[Greenwarden's Grove]] to watch over the Greenwarden.[[Who Wards The Greenwarden]] A portion of the Dragonmaw remained in the Wetlands. [[Prospector Whelgar]] asked adventurers to deal with the [[Angerfang]] [[Dragonmaw clan|Dragonmaw]] and their chief, [[Gorfax Angerfang]].[[The Angerfang Menace]] Meanwhile, numerous black [[whelp]]s led by the [[drake]] [[Pyrricion]] fought against the Dragonmaw orcs who sought to capture them, they were assisted by black [[dragonspawn]].[[The Crazed Dragonmaw]] After it was revealed that the [[Dark Iron dwarf|Dark Iron dwarves]] of Dun Modr were, in fact, loyal members of the [[Twilight's Hammer]].[[The Twilight's Hammer Revealed]] [[Thargas Anvilmar]] led Alliance heroes in driving them out, retaking [[Dun Modr]] for the [[Ironforge (kingdom)|kingdom of Ironforge]].[[The Battle of Thandol Span]] At the same time, [[Muradin Bronzebeard]] tasked [[Forba Slabchisel]] with leading the expedition sent to survey the damage that the [[Stonewrought Dam]]'s destruction caused on the Wetlands.[[Fight the Flood]] In time, the Twilight's Hammer under the service of [[Neltharion]] and [[Old God]]s, seized the fortress of [[Grim Batol]] as part of their expansion within the [[Twilight Highlands]] on the east, brutally pushing back the red flight's forces with the help of the [[black dragonflight]]. The red dragons eventually joined forces with the [[Alliance]] [[adventurer|forces]] for a unified attack on the ancient stronghold and ripped it free from the clutches of the Twilight's Hammer.{{Ref WoWCV3|208}} ==Getting there== ;{{Horde}}Horde: From [[Hammerfall]] in the [[Arathi Highlands]], run south/southwest to the large bridge, the [[Thandol Span]]. The Wetlands are on the other side. ;{{Alliance}}Alliance: From [[Ironforge]] go east through [[Dun Morogh]] to [[Loch Modan]]. Take the road in the Loch north to [[Dun Algaz]] in the Wetlands. You can also take the boat from [[Theramore]], which leads to [[Menethil Harbor]]. ==Geography== There are currently no dungeons or battlegrounds in this area. ===Maps and subregions=== A once thriving metropolis has all but been covered by the jungle. ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} Cold and drear, '''the Wetlands''' is [[Khaz Modan]]'s northernmost realm. It can be found after crossing through [[Loch Modan]]'s [[Dun Algaz Gate]]. Once dominated by [[Dwarf|dwarven]] strongholds, the Wetlands suffered grievously in the [[Second War|Second]] and [[Third War]]s. The strongholds have fallen, and wild creatures, [[murloc]]s and renegade [[orc]]s claim the land. The Wetlands is little more than a thoroughfare for travelers moving to and from [[Menethil Harbor]], the only safe settlement in the area. This marsh is not nearly as cheerful as Loch Modan.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 79 ===History=== [[Old Horde|Horde]] and [[Scourge]] forces devastated the Wetlands in the [[Second War|Second]] and [[Third War]]s, forcing the [[Ironforge (kingdom)|Ironforge]] dwarves to retreat to Loch Modan and [[Dun Morogh]]. [[Alliance]] forces have since established [[Menethil Harbor]], but the area is still wild and untamed. The Wetlands is a buffer zone between the inhabited Khaz Modan and Scourge-infested [[Lordaeron]].''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 80 Menethil Harbor, on the west coast, is the only Alliance settlement in the Wetlands. Menethil's people are tense and wary, as orcs and other creatures attack the walls constantly. [[Dark Iron dwarf|Dark Iron dwarves]] claimed the fallen city of [[Dun Modr]], in the north, as their own, while the renegade orcish [[Dragonmaw clan]], defeated shortly after the Second War, fled to this land. The orcs, still flying their white [[dragon]] banners, refuse to ally with [[Thrall]] and raid Menethil Harbor repeatedly. Disputed ruins dot the landscape, and murlocs, [[bog beast]]s and other creatures are perfect hunting targets. Menethil Harbor would be indebted to any intrepid individuals who eliminated the Dragonmaw threat. The Dark Iron dwarves of Dun Modr uncovered ancient writings in their ruined fortress that spoke of an artifact called [[Ironbeard's Axe]]. They leaked this information to both Menethil Harbor and the Dragonmaw orcs, and later planned to incite both factions to race to [[Ironbeard's Tomb]], fighting [[ooze]]s and each other in the process. In the aftermath, Dark Iron agents ambushed the victors on their way out, thereby claiming the magical axe for themselves. ===Geography=== The Wetlands is one vast, cold swamp stretching to Khaz Modan's northern coast. Gray mist cloaks the ground, giving the area an eerie, isolated feel, while the skies are constantly overcast. To the south are a series of one thousand stone steps carved into the rock, at the top of which is Dun Algaz Gate and the entrance to Loch Modan. To the north is Lordaeron's [[Arathi Highlands]]. Ruined dwarven fortresses can be seen, thrusting their bones up from the surrounding filth. Elevation rises to the east to the mountain fortress of [[Grim Batol]], and to the south toward Loch Modan. As if rebel orcs and Dark Iron dwarves were not bad enough, [[Bluegill tribe|Bluegill murlocs]], bog beasts, and oozes roam the murky landscape. Menethil Harbor is the only safe settlement in the Wetlands, though wrecked strongholds and other ruins draw treasure seekers to this bleak land. Many shipwrecks line the coast. Curious explorers could find many intriguing items in these shattered hulks.
